definitions.gloss: nothing at all; complete absence; nil
definitions.explanation: Emphatic way of saying there is absolutely nothing of something. Stronger than simply saying ない, it stresses the total lack or absence.

examples.japanese: ⟦{経験|けいけん}→経験：01179_keiken⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{皆無|かいむ}だ。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{犯罪|はんざい}→犯罪：03569_hanzai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{皆無|かいむ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{等|ひと}しい→等しい：03710_hitoshii⟧。
examples.english: Crime in this area is virtually nonexistent.

examples.japanese: ⟦{反対|はんたい}{意見|いけん}→反対意見：24246_hantaiiken⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{皆無|かいむ}だった⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{提案|ていあん}→提案：03536_teian⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦そのまま→そのまま：03322_sonomama⟧⟦{承認|しょうにん}→承認：03237_shounin⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Since there were no objections whatsoever, the proposal was approved as-is.

notes:
USAGE:
{皆無|かいむ} is a formal, emphatic expression. It is often used as a predicate ({皆無|かいむ}だ / {皆無|かいむ}⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧) or in the pattern {皆無|かいむ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{等|ひと}しい→等しい：03710_hitoshii⟧ ("virtually nonexistent").
More emphatic and literary than ⟦{全|まった}く→全く：02363_mattaku⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧. Often appears in written or formal spoken contexts such as reports, speeches, and news articles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {皆無|かいむ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{等|ひと}しい→等しい：03710_hitoshii⟧ (virtually nonexistent)
- {皆無|かいむ}⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧ (to be completely absent)
- ⟦{経験|けいけん}→経験：01179_keiken⟧{皆無|かいむ} (zero experience)
